subject: Recap: tool-calling integration options + failover patterns for Nimbus POC
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sam Holmes <sam.holmes@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: tool-calling integration options + failover patterns for Nimbus POC

Sam — thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed options so we can align on a technical POC: 

Key goals you reiterated:
- Improve triage & routing for inbound patient queries (reduce agent handoffs)
- Surface structured actions (schedule appt, fetch lab results) via tools rather than freeform text
- Keep PII inside Nimbus VPC where required; prefer customer-managed keys

High-level integration options (tradeoffs):
1) Client-side SDK + server adapter (fast integration, minimal infra change)
   - SDK in your app sends structured tool calls to a Redwood endpoint we host for you
   - Good for quick demo; requires secure key distribution and CORS considerations
2) Server-side proxy routing (recommended for production)
   - Your backend calls Redwood with a routing header (region/model variant). Backend handles auth exchange (OIDC) and returns structured tool outputs to clients
   - Enables stronger auditing and retention control in your VPC
3) Hybrid: local tool execution + Redwood for NLU/reranking
   - Use Redwood for intent/slot extraction and embeddings-based reranker, but call your internal services for sensitive actions (webhooks, calendar writes)

Tool/function-calling patterns we discussed:
- Define each tool with: name, input_schema (typed), timeout_ms, idempotency_hint, allowed_principals
- Fan-out pattern: parallelize non-conflicting tools (search + db_annotate) and join results with a reranker
- Fallbacks: model-based fallback -> cached response -> human-in-the-loop escalation

Attachments: I uploaded an initial mapping (nimbus-mapping-v1.xlsx) with example intents -> tools. Also attached a short patterns doc (redwood-integration-patterns.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
- We’ll provision a sandbox key with region=us-west and quota for the POC (you asked for a week-long test)
- Aisha will follow up with concrete tool-definition templates and an auth recommendation
- Please share a small sample dataset (anonymized) or traffic profile so we can size the capping/batching settings

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

— Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap: tool-calling integration options + failover patterns for Nimbus POC

Marcus — great summary, appreciate the clarity. A few quick clarifying questions before we start the POC: 

1) Auth: you mentioned customer-managed keys vs OIDC. For our security team, is there an option where Redwood never persists our long-lived keys? We prefer short-lived tokens (we run our own Okta).
2) Embeddings/reranker: our search infra currently returns 50 candidates. Would you recommend pushing vector search upstream and using Redwood only for reranking, or do both inside Redwood? Any concerns with token costs?
3) Tool safety: if the model calls a tool (e.g., cancel_appointment), how do you recommend limiting scope so it cannot call destructive actions by mistake?

Also — please provision the sandbox credentials (we can use them for initial smoke tests). Timeline: if we can start next Monday (06/22) and run three days of traffic, we can evaluate.

Thanks,
Sam Holmes
Head of Product
Nimbus Health
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Holmes <sam.holmes@nimbushealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: tool-calling integration options + failover patterns for Nimbus POC

Hi Sam — quick technical replies inline below and a pragmatic recommendation for the POC.

Auth: short-lived token pattern
- Recommendation: use an OIDC token exchange (Okta as IdP) -> Redwood accepts a short-lived access token (exp <= 15m) issued to your backend. Redwood will not store your long-lived creds; only a short-lived session token for the request lifecycle and auditing metadata (not raw secrets).
- For the sandbox we’ll issue an API key tied to the sandbox project but you can also test with a dev OIDC flow if you prefer.

Embeddings / Reranker pattern
- Option A (client-side search + Redwood rerank): you run vector search in your infra, send top-k to Redwood with passage content for reranking. Pros: avoids transferring corpus and reduces embedding compute on our side. Cons: you must send candidate content as input tokens (cost depends on candidate size).
- Option B (Redwood-hosted embedding store + rerank): Redwood computes embeddings and stores them (optionally in your VPC). Pros: simpler integration; we can do incremental updates and efficient nearest-neighbor queries. Cons: adds storage/ops overhead and cross-account data considerations.
- POC suggestion: start with Option A for speed — send top-20 candidates and evaluate reranking lift. If latency or token cost becomes an issue, iterate to Option B.

Tool safety and scoping
- Each tool definition should include an allowlist of user roles and a capability bitmask (read/write/admin) and a sandbox flag.
- At runtime we evaluate a policy engine: tool_allowed = tool.allowlist.contains(principal) && not_in_maintenance_mode(tool)
- For destructive tools, require a 2-step confirmation: first a dry-run response (structured) then an explicit confirm action signed by a second principal or UI button.

Example tool-definition (for POC) — this is a flat example you can paste into your config: 

name: "fetch_patient_summary"
input_schema: "{patient_id: string, window_days: int}"
timeout_ms: 2000
idempotency_hint: "patient_id|window_days"
allowed_principals: ["nimbus_backend"]
sandbox: true

Parallel tool pattern (when to fan-out)
- Use parallel calls when tools are orthogonal (e.g., semantic_search + external_lab_lookup).
- Limit concurrency per request (recommended: 3 parallel calls) and aggregate with a lightweight join step that calls the reranker.
- Enforce per-tool timeouts and an overall request budget (e.g., 3s). If the budget is exceeded, return best-effort partial structured output and escalate asynchronously to agents.

I attached a short patterns doc (redwood-integration-patterns.pdf) that includes sample server adapter code and a stubbed tool-definition YAML.

I’ll provision the sandbox keys and send them with the setup guide later today. We’ll also include a small Postman collection for smoke tests.

— Aisha
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap: tool-calling integration options + failover patterns for Nimbus POC

Sam — looping in next concrete steps and the POC runbook. Thanks Marcus & Aisha for the docs.

POC plan (3 business days)
Day 0 (prep): we’ll provision sandbox keys (region=us-west), provide Postman collection, and a redwood-sample-config.yml with two example tools: fetch_patient_summary, search_medical_notes. You’ll get the sandbox API key + an OIDC dev flow sample.
Day 1 (smoke tests): run 50 synthetic requests through your integration (client->your backend->Redwood). Validate: structured output shape, tool call logs, latency percentiles.
Day 2 (load + edge cases): send mixed payloads including long notes and malformed inputs to exercise timeouts and fallbacks. We’ll monitor rerank lift and token usage.
Day 3 (handoff): review results, map success criteria to your KPIs (reduction in agent escalations, accuracy of scheduled actions), and agree next steps (Dedicated evaluation if metrics look good).

Observability & error handling runbook (short):
- Per-request tracing header: X-Request-ID (UUID). Propagate to all tool calls.
- Idempotency: include idempotency_key for commands that mutate state.
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter for transient 5xx from internal tool endpoints. Cap retries to 2 attempts per tool.
- Circuit breaker: open circuit for a tool after 20 failures in a 5m window; while open return a safe fallback and create an async task for human review.
- Partial results policy: if more than 50% of fan-out tools fail, mark request as degraded and add a metadata flag for CS review.

Success criteria (suggested):
- Mean end-to-end latency < 1.5s for smoke profile
- Tool call success rate >= 99% under smoke load
- Reranker improves top-1 relevance by at least 12% over baseline vector-only scoring (measured on a small labeled set)

Action items:
- Marcus: share HubSpot deal link and grant sandbox access (in progress)
- Sam: confirm you’ll share an anonymized sample of 200 queries by EOD Mon (we can accept CSV)
- Aisha: send redwood-sample-config.yml and Postman collection (ETA: today)
- Neha: schedule a 30m tech-check on Tues 06/23 10:00am PT to validate OIDC exchange and smoke key usage

If that timeline works I’ll create the calendar invite and include the runbook doc.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Product Solutions — Redwood Inference
